# Anthropic may not secure an investment-grade rating after its IPO, Blackstone tells investors (FT, via headline relay)

**Vintage:** headlines 10/30 16:47–16:48 UTC citing the Financial Times. FT article not read.

**What is new versus SIG-W-20261016-008:** that card carried KBRA's June BB+ (top junk rung) and bankers' push for investment-grade ratings once Anthropic and OpenAI list. Today's relay reverses the expectation: Blackstone reportedly told investors Anthropic **may not** get investment grade after the IPO and is expected to receive a **"high" junk** rating. Moody's, S&P and Fitch had published no rating as of the 10/16 card.

**Why it matters:** rating grade sets which money can hold the debt behind AI-infrastructure financing (the $35B Apollo/Blackstone chip financing named in 016). A junk outcome keeps that paper in private-credit and high-yield hands rather than investment-grade portfolios.

**ACTION BROCK:** integrate as a financing-leg update; confirm against the FT body or an agency publication before grading. **INFO VULCAN** (capex substance), **LIQUID** (credit-market absorption), **RED** (BOARD pull).

**Limits:** two headlines; FT body, any agency action and the exact rating scale unread.
